name: MCP4725 12-bit I2C DAC
description: Microchip 12-bit digital-to-analog converter with I2C interface and EEPROM. Outputs a rail-to-rail voltage of VDD x code / 4096 (0 to VDD, the supply is the reference). Runs on 2.7-5.5 V. Sold as: Adafruit MCP4725 Breakout Board - 12-Bit DAC with I2C Interface, STEMMA QT (product 935; 6-pin header VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, A0, VOUT; MCP4725A1, I2C address 0x62, 0x63 with A0 high).
eli5: Lets your board make a steady voltage anywhere between 0 V and its supply, set by a number from 0 to 4095.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 2.7-5.5 V; also the DAC reference, so Vout full scale = VIN. Use the microcontroller's logic voltage.

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (10 k pull-up on the board)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (10 k pull-up on the board)

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Address select: low (pulled down on the board) = 0x62, high = 0x63

pins.name: VOUT
pins.description: DAC analog output, 0 V to VIN (keep load above 5 kOhm)

buildNotes: Vout = VIN x code / 4096, so the output range follows the supply: 0-3.3 V on 3.3 V, 0-5 V on 5 V.
Fast write: two bytes [0 0 PD1 PD0 D11-D8][D7-D0]. Command 0x40 writes the DAC register, 0x60 writes it and the EEPROM (up to 50 ms, poll RDY/BSY bit 7 of the first read byte).
The Adafruit board uses the MCP4725A1: address 0x62 with A0 low (default), 0x63 with A0 high or the back jumper closed.
Do not write the EEPROM in a loop: it is rated for about 1 million writes.
Power VIN from the same voltage as the microcontroller's logic so the I2C pull-ups match.

driver.code:
# MCP4725 12-bit I2C DAC (Microchip MCP4725), MicroPython driver.
# Commands from the Microchip datasheet DS22039D, section 6:
#   Fast mode write (C2 C1 = 0 0): [0 0 PD1 PD0 D11-D8] [D7-D0]
#   Write DAC register (C2 C1 C0 = 0 1 0): [0x40 | PD1 PD0 << 1] [D11-D4] [D3-D0 0000]
#   Write DAC register and EEPROM (0 1 1): [0x60 | PD << 1] [D11-D4] [D3-D0 0000], EEPROM write takes up to 50 ms
#   Read: 5 bytes [RDY/BSY POR x x x PD1 PD0 x] [D11-D4] [D3-D0 xxxx] [x PD1 PD0 x D11-D8] [D7-D0]
# Vout = VDD * code / 4096 (the supply is the reference).
import time

# Power-down modes (PD1 PD0): 0 normal, 1 = 1 kOhm, 2 = 100 kOhm, 3 = 500 kOhm to ground
PD_NORMAL = 0
PD_1K = 1
PD_100K = 2
PD_500K = 3


class MCP4725:
    def __init__(self, i2c, addr=0x62, vdd=3.3):
        """addr 0x62 with A0 low, 0x63 with A0 high (MCP4725A1, as on the Adafruit board).
        vdd: the supply voltage on VIN, which is the DAC's full-scale reference."""
        self.i2c = i2c
        self.addr = addr
        self.vdd = vdd

    def write(self, code, power_down=PD_NORMAL):
        """Fast-mode write of a 12-bit code (0-4095) to the DAC register. EEPROM is not changed."""
        code = max(0, min(4095, int(code)))
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([((power_down & 3) << 4) | (code >> 8), code & 0xFF]))

    def write_eeprom(self, code, power_down=PD_NORMAL):
        """Write the code to the DAC register AND the EEPROM (the value used at power-up)."""
        code = max(0, min(4095, int(code)))
        self.i2c.writeto(self.addr, bytes([0x60 | ((power_down & 3) << 1), code >> 4, (code & 0x0F) << 4]))
        # RDY/BSY stays low until the EEPROM write is done (typ 25 ms, max 50 ms)
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while not self.read()[3]:
            if time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) > 100:
                raise OSError('MCP4725 EEPROM write timed out')
            time.sleep_ms(5)

    def set_voltage(self, volts):
        """Set the output in volts (0 to vdd)."""
        self.write(round(volts * 4096 / self.vdd))

    def power_down(self, mode=PD_500K):
        """Switch the output off; it is pulled to ground through 1k/100k/500k."""
        self.write(0, mode)

    def read(self):
        """Return (dac_code, power_down, eeprom_code, ready)."""
        b = self.i2c.readfrom(self.addr, 5)
        dac = (b[1] << 4) | (b[2] >> 4)
        pd = (b[0] >> 1) & 3
        eeprom = ((b[3] & 0x0F) << 8) | b[4]
        ready = bool(b[0] & 0x80)
        return dac, pd, eeprom, ready

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin, ADC
import time
from mcp4725 import MCP4725

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
dac = MCP4725(i2c, 0x62, vdd=3.3)
adc = ADC(Pin({VOUT}))

def vout():
    time.sleep_ms(20)  # let the output and the ADC settle
    return adc.read_u16() * 3.3 / 65535

while True:
    for code in (1000, 3000):
        dac.write(code)
        v = vout()
        print('code=%d Vout=%.1fV' % (dac.read()[0], v))  # 0.1 V: the board ADC reads within a few mV
    dac.power_down()
    print('off Vout=%.1fV' % vout())
    time.sleep(1)
